## 32.1 The Contribution Workflow

Beyond creating new packages, filling the Julia geospatial gap requires contributing to existing packages. GeoDataFrames.jl needs better overlay operation coverage. GeoMakie.jl needs a native choropleth classification integration. ArchGDAL.jl needs higher-level topology operations. This section covers the professional contribution workflow for JuliaGeo packages, from opening an issue through CI passing and merge.

```julia
# === Contributing to GeoDataFrames.jl: Adding st_difference ===

# Step 1: Fork and clone the repository
# git clone https://github.com/yourusername/GeoDataFrames.jl.git
# git checkout -b feature/st_difference

# Step 2: Add the feature — src/GeoDataFrames.jl
"""
    st_difference(gdf_a, gdf_b)
```

Compute geometric difference: geometry A minus the intersection with geometry B.

Returns a GeoDataFrame with the same schema as gdf_a.

```julia
# Example
# (example: julia)
county_area = st_difference(counties, hpsa_zones)
# (end example)
"""
function st_difference(gdf_a::DataFrame, gdf_b::DataFrame)
    # Dissolve gdf_b into a single geometry for subtraction
    b_union = ArchGDAL.union([GeoInterface.convert(ArchGDAL.IGeometry, g)
                               for g in gdf_b.geometry]...)

    result_geoms = map(gdf_a.geometry) do geom_a
        a = GeoInterface.convert(ArchGDAL.IGeometry, geom_a)
        ArchGDAL.difference(a, b_union)
    end

    result = copy(gdf_a)
    result.geometry = result_geoms
    return result
end

# Step 3: Add tests — test/test_overlay.jl
@testset "st_difference" begin
    # Simple case: rectangle minus overlapping rectangle
    rect_a = _make_rect(0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0)
    rect_b = _make_rect(5.0, 0.0, 15.0, 10.0)
    gdf_a  = DataFrame(id=1, geometry=[rect_a])
    gdf_b  = DataFrame(id=2, geometry=[rect_b])
    result = st_difference(gdf_a, gdf_b)
    # Expected: 5×10 = 50 sq units (left half of rect_a)
    @test isapprox(ArchGDAL.getarea(result.geometry[1]), 50.0; atol=1e-6)

    # Edge case: no overlap
    rect_c = _make_rect(20.0, 0.0, 30.0, 10.0)
    gdf_c  = DataFrame(id=3, geometry=[rect_c])
    result2 = st_difference(gdf_a, gdf_c)
    @test isapprox(ArchGDAL.getarea(result2.geometry[1]), 100.0; atol=1e-6)

    # Edge case: complete containment
    rect_d = _make_rect(-1.0, -1.0, 11.0, 11.0)
    gdf_d  = DataFrame(id=4, geometry=[rect_d])
    result3 = st_difference(gdf_a, gdf_d)
    @test ArchGDAL.getarea(result3.geometry[1]) < 1e-6
end

# Step 4: Update CHANGELOG.md
# ## [Unreleased]
# ### Added
# - `st_difference(gdf_a, gdf_b)`: compute geometric difference

# Step 5: Open PR with template
# Title: "feat: add st_difference overlay operation"
# Body: closes #issue_number, description, example, test coverage
```


## 32.2 Extending GeoStats.jl for Healthcare Kriging

GeoStats.jl is the most mature geostatistics package in Julia and is actively developed by Júlio Hoffimann. It supports kriging — spatial interpolation that produces smoothed continuous surfaces from point-sampled data. For healthcare, kriging is valuable for interpolating provider density surfaces, environmental exposure estimates, and small-area health outcome estimates to arbitrary spatial resolutions. This example extends GeoStats.jl with a healthcare-specific covariance function.

```julia
# === Extending GeoStats.jl: Healthcare variogram fitting ===
using GeoStats, GeoTables, DataFrames

"""
    fit_healthcare_variogram(df, var; max_lag=200.0)

Fit an empirical variogram and select the best theoretical model
for a healthcare variable (e.g., provider density, CVD rate).
Automatically tests Spherical, Exponential, Gaussian models.
Returns best-fit variogram model by Weighted Least Squares.
"""
function fit_healthcare_variogram(
        df::DataFrame,
        var::Symbol;
        max_lag::Float64 = 200.0,  # km
        nlags::Int = 30
    )
    # GeoStats expects a GeoTable — wrap DataFrame with geometry
    gt = GeoTable(df; geometry=:geom_col)

    # Empirical variogram
    γ_emp = EmpiricalVariogram(gt, var;
        nlags  = nlags,
        maxlag = max_lag * 1000  # convert km to m
    )

    # Fit three theoretical models and compare WLS error
    models = [SphericalVariogram, ExponentialVariogram, GaussianVariogram]
    fitted = [fit(M, γ_emp) for M in models]
    wls_errors = [sum((γ_emp.ordinate .- fitted[k](γ_emp.abscissa)).^2 ./
                       max.(γ_emp.counts, 1))
                  for k in 1:length(models)]
    best_idx = argmin(wls_errors)

    @info "Best variogram model: $(models[best_idx]) (WLS=$(round(wls_errors[best_idx];digits=3)))"
    return fitted[best_idx]
end

"""
    kriging_surface(df, var, target_grid; variogram=nothing)
```

Ordinary kriging interpolation of a healthcare variable to a target grid.

df:           Source data (county-level or point-sampled)

var:          Variable to interpolate (e.g., :cvd_rate)

target_grid:  Cartesian2D grid at desired output resolution

Returns GeoTable with kriged estimates and kriging variance.

"""

```julia
function kriging_surface(
        df::DataFrame,
        var::Symbol,
        target_grid;
        variogram = nothing
    )
    gt = GeoTable(df; geometry=:geom_col)
    γ  = isnothing(variogram) ? fit_healthcare_variogram(df, var) : variogram

    problem  = EstimationProblem(gt, target_grid, var)
    solver   = Kriging(var => (variogram=γ, mean=mean(df[!, var])))
    solution = solve(problem, solver)

    return solution
end
```
